play.name: Play
play.about: Games and the places they live

apps.name: Tide
apps.summary: Your music, from everywhere you keep it
desc: Tide plays the music on this computer and on your own music server in one library. The album that's playing lights the window, and the queue survives a restart.
Gapless playback, a mini player in the Shelf, and the same library on your phone.

items: Crossfade between tracks, from off to 12 seconds
Albums from a Navidrome server load twice as fast

reviews: Finally, my Navidrome server and my laptop in one place. The album colour thing is gorgeous.
Gapless playback that actually works. The queue survives a restart.
Lovely. I want smart playlists next.
Crossfade at 6 seconds is perfect for long runs.
Missing lyrics, but everything else beats what I used before.
The mini player in the Shelf is all I need most of the day.
My FLAC library finally looks like a record shelf.
reach: Reads it to build your library
Only if you add one, like Navidrome
Nothing about what you play leaves this computer

apps.name: Photos
apps.summary: Every photo you've taken, beautifully kept
desc: Your photos by day, month and year, with the places and the people in them. Memories gathers a weekend or a trip without being asked.
Edits are kept beside the original, so you can always go back.
reviews: Years view is the best way to scroll through ten years of photos I have used.
Found every photo from our trip by typing “beach 2024”.
Fast with 60,000 photos. I would like albums to sort by date.
Edits sync to my phone before I pick it up.
reach: Read from the photos themselves; nothing is uploaded

apps.name: Filer
apps.summary: Files, with a tray you can carry
desc: Your files and drives, with a tray that holds what you're moving between folders and windows. Filer comes with Luma and updates with it.

apps.name: Write
apps.summary: Documents, beautifully set and easy to share
desc: A word processor that sets your text well without a ribbon. Opens and saves Word documents, exports to PDF, and shares a live copy anyone can read in a browser.
reach: Only the ones you open or save
reviews: Opens my Word files and they look right. That alone sold me.
Lovely to write in. Track changes needs a filter for one person.
The outline on the left keeps a 90-page report under control.

apps.name: Viola
desc: The web, with tabs in a sidebar you can name and keep. Viola comes with Luma and updates with it.

apps.name: Messages
desc: Messages and calls, end-to-end encrypted, on your own Luma network. Your @username finds people; your number never has to.
reach: Only during a call you start or answer
reviews: Texts from my Android phone right on the laptop.
Group calls just work. No account to make.

apps.name: Notes
apps.summary: Catch a thought, share it with anyone
desc: Notes that open where you left off. Checklists, pictures and links; share one with a link anyone can open.
reach: Your notes stay in your account
reviews: Quick, quiet, and the search is instant.
Shared notes with my partner for groceries. It just updates.
I want tags as well as folders.

apps.name: Calendar
apps.summary: See what's next and when you're free
desc: Your calendars side by side. Type an event the way you'd say it and the bar becomes the event.
reviews: Typing “lunch with Ana fri 1pm” and having it appear is magic.
Week view is great. Time zones could be clearer.

apps.name: Contacts
apps.summary: Everyone you know, in one place

apps.name: Charlie
apps.summary: Mail, with the noise turned down
desc: Mail from all your accounts in one inbox. People you write to come first; newsletters and receipts wait in their own place. Replies grow out of the bar.
reach: For mail from people you know

apps.name: YouTube
desc: A YouTube client in Luma's own parts: the video leads, Up next sits beside it, and it keeps your place across the desktop, a tablet and your phone.

apps.name: Maps
apps.summary: Find your way, without being followed
desc: Maps and directions with no account. Your searches and trips stay on this computer.
reach: Only while you ask for it

apps.name: Weather
reach: If you let it, for local weather

apps.name: Clock
apps.summary: Alarms, timers and the time anywhere

apps.name: Camera
apps.summary: Photos and video from any camera

apps.name: Memo
apps.summary: Voice notes that write themselves down
desc: Record a thought and read it back: every memo is transcribed on this computer, nothing is uploaded.

apps.name: Monitor
apps.summary: What the computer is doing, right now

apps.name: Ari
desc: Ari answers questions, finds things across your apps and does small jobs for you. It runs on this computer; when a question needs the internet, it says so and asks.

apps.name: Canvas
apps.summary: Design anything, from posters to apps
desc: Layouts, illustrations and prototypes on one infinite canvas, with real type and real colour.
reach: Only the ones you open or save

apps.name: Grid
reach: Only the ones you open or save

apps.name: Stage
reach: Only the ones you open or save

apps.name: Sessions
desc: A recording studio: record takes, arrange them on a timeline and mix with real-time effects. Works with any audio interface Luma sees.
reach: Only the ones you open or save

apps.name: Darkroom
desc: Raw development with film looks you can tune, and edits that never touch the original.

apps.name: Reel
apps.summary: Edit video on a timeline that stays out of the way
desc: Cut, trim and grade on a magnetic timeline; export for anywhere you post.
reach: Only the ones you open or save

apps.name: Vault
desc: Your passwords and passkeys, end-to-end encrypted and synced through your Connect account. It fills them in for you in Viola and in apps.
reach: Only to fill them when you ask

apps.name: Blender
desc: Modelling, sculpting, animation, rendering, compositing and video editing in one application.
reviews: Runs better here than on my old Windows install. Cycles finds the GPU on its own.
Sculpting with a pen tablet feels smooth.
Installed in a minute. Took a restart before Cycles saw my second GPU.
Same files as my Windows machine, no conversion.
reach: Opens and saves wherever you choose

apps.name: GIMP
desc: Retouching, compositing and painting with layers, masks and filters.
reach: Only the ones you open or save
reviews: Does everything I need. Still learning where things are.
Opens big PSDs without a fuss.

apps.name: Inkscape
reach: Only the ones you open or save

apps.name: Krita
desc: A painting application with brush engines, a wrap-around mode and animation, made by and for artists.
reach: Only the ones you open or save
reviews: Pressure on my tablet worked first try.
The best free painting app, and it feels at home here.

apps.name: Kdenlive
reach: Only the ones you open or save

apps.name: Audacity
reach: Only the ones you open or save

apps.name: OBS Studio
desc: Capture your screen, windows and cameras, mix scenes, and record or stream them.
reach: When you add a screen or window source
reviews: Records my screen and webcam without dropped frames.

apps.name: VLC
reach: Only the ones you open or save
reviews: Works on the TV too. The remote layout is a bit small.

apps.name: Spotify
reviews: Works fine. Media keys and the Shelf player both control it.
Same as on any other computer, which is what I wanted.
Sometimes forgets my login after an update.

apps.name: Discord

items: A fix for sharing your screen

reviews: Screen share with sound works. Finally.
Notifications land in the right place. Updates are frequent.

apps.name: Signal
desc: Messages, voice and video calls, end-to-end encrypted, from a non-profit.
reviews: Linked to my phone in ten seconds.
Private and simple. Nothing to complain about.

apps.name: LibreOffice
desc: Writer, Calc, Impress and Draw: documents, spreadsheets and presentations that open and save Microsoft Office files.
reach: Only the ones you open or save
reviews: Opens everything. Looks a little old next to Luma’s apps.
Our whole office uses it. No licences to buy.

apps.name: Obsidian
reach: The folder you choose for your notes
reviews: My vault opened untouched. Plugins all work.
Great. I wish it used the Luma file picker.

apps.name: Steam
desc: Your Steam library on Luma. Most Windows games run through Proton without changes.
reach: It comes off the next time you restart after removing it
reviews: Most of my library runs with no tweaking.
A couple of anti-cheat games won’t start, which is not Luma’s fault.
Big Picture on the TV is a great couch setup.

apps.name: VSCodium
reach: Only the ones you open or save
Runs the commands you type in it

apps.name: Nextcloud
apps.summary: Sync your files with your own server

apps.name: Bitwarden
apps.summary: A password manager you can host

apps.name: Firefox
reviews: Hardware video decoding is on out of the box.
Works great. Viola is faster for me, but I keep this for work.

apps.name: Heroic
apps.summary: Your Epic, GOG and Amazon games

apps.name: nvtop
apps.summary: Graphics card activity in the terminal

looks.name: Luma
looks.line: Soft glass, round corners and one bright key
looks.about: The way Luma comes: translucent windows over your wallpaper, rounded corners, and a single bright button for the thing you came to do.

looks.name: Cupertino
looks.line: Light windows, three coloured dots and a quiet grey
looks.about: Light, airy windows with the close, minimise and zoom dots on the left and the title in the middle. Calm greys and a blue accent.

looks.name: Redmond
looks.line: Square-ish windows, controls on the right, a soft frosted sheet
looks.about: Windows with gently squared corners, the controls on the right and a frosted sheet behind the content. Familiar from the first click.

looks.name: Exile
looks.line: Black title bars, bevelled grey and a 1990s workstation
looks.about: A tribute to the black-and-grey workstations of the early 90s: bevelled buttons, black title bars and not a gradient in sight.

looks.line: Navy title bars, chunky bevels, teal desktop. Start me up
looks.about: Gray bevelled windows, navy title bars and a teal desktop. Everything a little chunkier, everything exactly where you remember it.

looks.name: Ember
looks.line: A slow coal glow that warms the whole shell
looks.about: Deep oranges at the bottom of the screen, cooling to plum at the top. Your windows pick up a little of the warmth.

looks.name: Blue Fog
looks.line: Cool, quiet and easy on tired eyes
looks.about: Soft blues with nothing sharp in them. It stays out of the way of whatever you are doing.

looks.name: D-Ink
looks.line: Paper and ink, three line weights, nothing tinted. Made for e-paper, lovely anywhere
looks.about: Black ink on warm paper. No colour, no shadows, three weights of line. Built for e-paper screens, and calm on any screen.

looks.name: Meadow
looks.line: Morning grass for the light appearance
looks.about: Fresh grass under a pale sky, made for the light appearance.

looks.name: Prism
looks.about: The ribbon of colour Luma started with. It looks good in the dark and the light appearance.

looks.name: Studio Night
looks.line: A deep plum appearance with a matching wallpaper and accent
looks.about: A plum appearance with a matching wallpaper and accent colour, for late work in a dim room.

looks.name: Pebble
looks.line: Every app icon as a smooth river stone
looks.about: Every app icon, redrawn as a smooth stone in quiet colours. The shapes stay the same, so you still find things.

looks.name: Soft Keys
looks.line: Gentle clicks, chimes and alerts recorded on wood
looks.about: Clicks, chimes and alerts recorded on wooden blocks. Quieter than the defaults, and easier to live with.

looks.name: Atkinson Hyperlegible
looks.line: A typeface drawn for low vision, set as the system font
looks.about: A typeface designed so each letter is hard to mistake for another. Set across Luma as the system font.

looks.name: Dusk Pointers
looks.line: Rounded pointers with a soft shadow, in six sizes
looks.about: Rounded pointers with a soft shadow, in six sizes, so it is easy to find on a big screen.

tweaks.name: Battery Care
tweaks.line: Stops charging at 80% while you are plugged in all day
tweaks.about: Batteries wear out fastest when they sit at 100%. Battery Care holds yours at 80% while you are plugged in, and charges to full when you unplug.
tweaks.onTxt: Charging stops at 80% while plugged in

tweaks.name: Android Apps
tweaks.line: Run Android apps in a window, beside your Luma apps
tweaks.about: Install Android apps from Depot and run them in their own windows, next to your Luma apps.
tweaks.onTxt: Android apps open in windows like any other app

tweaks.name: Hot Corners
tweaks.line: Push the pointer into a corner to show windows, the desktop or Now
tweaks.about: Push the pointer into a corner of the screen to show all your windows, the desktop, or Now.
tweaks.onTxt: Each corner opens something you choose

tweaks.name: Three-finger Peek
tweaks.line: Rest three fingers on the touchpad to see under every window
tweaks.about: Rest three fingers on the touchpad and every window turns see-through, so you can see what is underneath.
tweaks.onTxt: Three fingers show what is under your windows

tweaks.name: Compose Key
tweaks.line: Caps Lock becomes Compose: type é, ñ, — and → in two keys
tweaks.about: Caps Lock becomes a Compose key. Press it, then two keys, to type characters like é, ñ, — and →.
tweaks.onTxt: Caps Lock then e and ’ types é

tweaks.name: Now Playing on Lock
tweaks.line: Big album art and controls on the lock screen while music plays
tweaks.about: While music plays, the lock screen shows the album cover large, with play, skip and volume.
tweaks.off: A small player on the lock screen

tweaks.name: Pi-hole Tile
tweaks.line: Pause your Pi-hole for five minutes from Quick Options
tweaks.about: Adds a Pi-hole tile to Quick Options, so you can pause ad blocking for five minutes when a site needs it.

tweaks.name: Studio Layouts
tweaks.line: Tiling layouts for wide monitors: 3 columns, focus and stage
tweaks.about: Layouts for wide monitors: three columns, one big window in the middle, or a stage with the rest to the side.

tweaks.name: Seconds in the Shelf
tweaks.about: The clock in the Shelf shows seconds as well as hours and minutes.

today.blurb: Start an album at your desk, keep it going on your phone, finish it on the TV. One library, no subscriptions.
Laptops that live on a charger wear their battery out fastest. Battery Care holds it at 80% until you unplug.
